Senses.Explanation: An egret is the white water bird repeatedly placed among snow, moonlight, white reeds, lotus, and mist in Chan verse and hall imagery. Danxia Zichun says an egret standing in snow is not the same color and pairs moonlight with reed flowers in a similar distinction. Changqing Huileng puts the bird into a reed-flower thicket where snow and moon together still do not reach it. Other poems retain the literal bird's flight, stance, fishing, and pale surroundings. The recurring white-on-white comparison makes sameness-with-difference observable without replacing the animal.
